correctness.rationale: Every labeled connected simple graph of orders two through five, seed set, legal homophilic rewire and breakpoint/open-cell threshold is checked exactly in verify.py, giving 213,990 nontrivial rewire comparisons and none increasing final adoption. Critical fractions k/d completely partition the continuum of real thresholds since all degrees are <=4. The explicit pair of 6-vertex trees has final adopted sets {1,2,3} and {0,1,2,3,4,5} for every the threshold interval from one third up to one half (exclusive); attaching leaves to the initial adopter 3 extends the strict gain to every larger size. The one-round monotonic obstruction is directly proved. Independent verification of the package is not claimed.

The present cutoff is narrower in dynamics but exhaustive in graph topology.

originality.rationale: The motivating Min--San Miguel 2023 article reports nonmonotone large-network promotion/suppression from adaptive rewiring, while this theorem proves a new sharp universal finite minimum for a single homophilic rewire and fixed seeds/strict fractional threshold. The 2018 noisy/absolute-threshold long-tie results do not cover this minimal connected graph invariant. Primary-source and research-record searches show no direct equivalent; residual priority uncertainty is disclosed.
residual_risks: Publication-priority searches are necessarily nonexhaustive; a separately phrased earlier six-vertex invariant may exist.

Exact enumeration depends on the openly supplied finite checker; independent implementation of the finite census has not been performed.

value.rationale: The exact smallest connected-network order supporting a rewiring-enhanced social adoption cascade is a natural boundary question given that the motivating 2023 model shows a qualitative competition between rewiring suppression and promotion. The complete all-graph cutoff, all-real-threshold proof, robust parameter interval [1/3,1/2), and every-size tree extension identify an elementary minimal mechanism that numerical large-random-graph phase plots cannot isolate; this is not an arbitrary finite calculation or a routine reparameterization.
